name: What the Old Man Kept (Quy Khư Di Vật)

bonuses.rule: when the Vase spills, the foe's clock stops for 2 s while yours runs (its arts, basic attack and companions wait, and its stacks do not count down), and each art you fire in those seconds lays one stack of every element you own on the foe.

story: Not made together: a vase from the year 0 and a bead from 400, kept by one man, which have learned to work as one because nothing else has stayed with him that long. Hermits make no regalia; this is what a life leaves. He wears the Primordial Mirror beside them.

name: The Lone Crane's Things (Cô Hạc Tam Vật)

bonuses.rule: while all three are worn, Lone Crane's sleeping rule wakes in any hand: each crit you land (instead of each attack you evade) sends one afterimage cut back along the same line, at most once a second.

story: The sword and the bone came to him together from his master at dawn in 900; the robe is his own. No one made them a set: he found that with the bone on his chest the sword half-wakes, and he has never taken it off.

name: The Still Pool (Đàm Ảnh Tam Vật)

bonuses.rule: the first art the foe aims at you in a fight is heard before it lands: you evade it and answer with a tide palm that lays two Water stacks. Each Thunder strike you take restores 3 % of your linh lực.

story: His master's robe, the mirror that took the bolt, and the bell he sank in the pool after he went blind. Gathered by grief, not made; whole while he sits by the water.
